Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::host¶

Back to Timeline Index Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

std::vector<std::int64_t> Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::host() const

What It Does¶

Materializes the time axis as raw epoch-nanosecond ticks on the host.

Use this when you need to hand the timestamps to a lower-level C++ algorithm, serialize them in your own format, or compare exact machine-time values without going through text formatting.

This is the machine-facing export, not the human-facing one.

Returns¶

std::vector<std::int64_t> The index values as epoch nanoseconds.

Examples¶

Example 1. Export exact machine-time ticks from the index.

auto ticks = idx.host();
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < ticks.size(); ++i) {
    if (i != 0) std::cout << ", ";
    std::cout << ticks[i];
}
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[
  1730419200000000000,
  1730420400000000000,
  1730421600000000000,
  1730422800000000000,
  1730424000000000000
]

Example 2. Hand those ticks to a lower-level serializer or C++ kernel.

std::vector<std::int64_t> ticks = idx.host();
// write ticks.data() and ticks.size() to your sink

Notes¶

  • host() gives exact machine-time values, not formatted strings.

  • For human-readable rendering, prefer idx.timeline().strftime(...) or idx.timeline().to_note_iso().

  • The returned values are UTC epoch nanoseconds internally.

  • Reach for this when exact comparison or foreign-code interoperability matters more than readability.

See Also¶

  • Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::timeline: work with the same axis as a Timeline.

  • Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::size: count the number of ticks before exporting.
